quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Can stop faster than regular cars.
Do not need more space to turn than regular cars.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Do not drive in these areas. Trucks are bigger and heavier, so they need more space to turn and stop than regular cars.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: The bigger the vehicle, the bigger the blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas behind them that the driver cannot see in the side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road and objects better.

questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. Drive slowly and carefully in fog. Do not use high beam headlights. Use low beams instead, as they work better in foggy conditions.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal any time you move left or right. Signal when entering traffic from a parking space, moving to a new lane, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: When someone is tailgating you:

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If there is no right lane, wait until the road ahead is clear and slowly reduce your speed to let them pass.

questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating and a right lane is open, move over. If there is no right lane, wait until the road ahead is clear and slowly reduce your speed. This lets them pass safely. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: Driving at night requires more caution because:

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: At night it is dark, so drivers cannot see as well as during the day. Use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, or any time you cannot see objects 500 feet away.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, other drivers must account for:

options.text: The extra distance large trucks need to stop.
The shorter distance large trucks need to stop.
The quieter noise large trucks make.
The higher speed of large trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: The extra distance large trucks need to stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop. Stay in places where the truck driver can see you. Do not block your view of traffic with the truck.

questions.question: You can legally pass on the right side of another vehicle if:

options.text: The vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an open passing lane.
You drive off the pavement to do so.
You are on a narrow bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an open passing lane.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right if there is an open lane and the vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You can also pass on the right on roads with two or more lanes going the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.

questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices tell you to. Not all crossings have lights or gates. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of danger. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give instructions.

questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances when they use sirens or air horns and red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions they give over their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only move when you are sure the way is clear.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in rain?
questions.explanation: In rainy conditions, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Do not make a right turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means the road ahead becomes a divided highway. Stay to the right of the divider or median.

questions.question: How far in advance should you signal before turning right or left?
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. This gives other drivers time to react to your movements. You can use your turn signals or hand signals.

questions.question: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop if:

options.text: You need to avoid hitting another vehicle.
You need to let passengers out.
You stop for less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You need to avoid hitting another vehicle.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down to reduce the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when changing lanes?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Check for other drivers in the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police about the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police about the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and use your turn signal. Look for other drivers moving into your lane. Never use your cell phone while driving to check if the road is clear.

questions.question: What should you do when you see or hear an emergency vehicle?

options.text: Stop right away and let the vehicle pass.
Drive to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, drive as far to the right as you safely can and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. This applies on all roads, no matter which direction the vehicle is coming from.

questions.question: When driving near pedestrians, what must a driver do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are jaywalking.
Give the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk your horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are jaywalking.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. It is your job as a driver to watch for pedestrians and let them cross, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: There is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line in the center. The broken line is on your side. When can you pass?

options.text: When the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass. You may cross the line to pass only if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is moving toward you. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: You are driving uphill and see a heavy truck ahead. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to pass the truck safely.
You may not be able to pass the truck legally.

questions.explanation: Large trucks often go slower than the speed limit, especially uphill. Be careful when following them. When visibility is limited on a hill, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.
